title: The Fool Says There Is No God
summary: The psalm describes the fool who says in his heart that there is no God, and then widens the view: the LORD looks down from heaven and finds that all have turned away and become corrupt. Evildoers devour God's people like bread, yet they will be overwhelmed with dread, because God stands with the righteous and is the refuge of the poor. It closes with a longing for Israel's salvation to come from Zion.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 14
from.text: Psalm 14 blends wisdom reflection with prophetic accusation and communal lament

line: The fool lives as if God will never judge; the LORD looks down and finds that all have turned aside, yet he stands with the righteous and shelters the poor.
guide: Ask where you live as if God does not see; most believers keep rooms like that. Then pray verse 7 for everyone who waits for God to put things right.

stanzas.title: God looks down: no one does good
The oppressors and the God who shelters the poor
A longing for salvation from Zion

verses.t: For the choirmaster. Of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their acts are vile. There is no one who does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon the LORD.
There they are, overwhelmed with dread, for God is in the company of the righteous.
You sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, yet the LORD is their shelter.
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When the LORD restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
